card.title: Diagnosing Power Draws on Nintendo Switch

source.title: Diagnosing Power Draws on Nintendo Switch

claims.statement: Bench-supply diagnosis without a battery: bypass the temp sensor with a 10k resistor at the battery test pads and feed 4.2 V at 2 A into the BQ24193 VBAT pad; less than 2 A will not reach second-stage boot.
First-stage check: 4.2 V at 1 A into VSYS (coil beside BQ24193); a maxed-out current means a short, otherwise check VCORE rails near MAX77620 and the 3.3 V regulator.
claims.evidence: Only time VSYS is used instead of VBAT.

claims.statement: On power button press a healthy board draws about 195 mA; 100–130 mA points at MAX77621 or MAX77812; no draw points at MAX77620.
Working boot: about 100 mA, then 150 mA hold, then 500–800 mA with LCD (400–500 mA without LCD).
A climb to 400–500 mA with the LCD connected but no picture suggests backlight or backlight driver TPS61163A.
M92T36 faults often show 400–800 mA dropping quickly to 200 mA in a loop; removing M92T36 and PI3USB and seeing a boot confirms one of them.
A steady 300 mA with no movement often means PI3USB30532 shorted the 3.3 V rail after USB-C damage sent 15 V into it.
Sitting at about 100 mA (sometimes creeping to 160 mA and back) points at MAX77621 or a damaged/missing MAX17050 fuel gauge circuit.
180–250 mA without reaching second-stage boot often indicates eMMC failure; audio and Wi-Fi IC faults can mimic this.
claims.evidence: eMMC profile; check RCM/APX with a payload injector and Hekate.

procedure: Remove battery; fit 10k resistor across the battery thermistor test pads.
Set bench supply 4.2 V / 1 A on VSYS for first-stage short check.
Move to VBAT on BQ24193 at 4.2 V / 2 A and press power; watch the draw pattern.
Match the draw to the profiles (195 mA ok first stage; 100 mA stall; 300 mA PI3USB; looping 400-800 mA M92T36; 180-250 mA eMMC).
For suspected eMMC, enter RCM, load Hekate, check fuel gauge and eMMC benchmark, ensure AutoRCM is off.

measurements.context: 2 A limit required for second-stage boot

card.caveats: Draw figures assume the guide's bench setup (no battery, 4.2 V on VBAT). Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
